Before the additives, there's the gel.
HDD Gel is the base bentonite in the Blick Fluids range. First thing in the tank.

What it does: builds a thin wall on the bore so it holds shape. Suspends cuttings so they come out the hole instead of settling on the low side. Cools and lubes the bit.

Get the gel right and the rest of the program works. Get it wrong and you spend the day chasing problems no additive will fix.

Friday we'll go deeper. When to push the gel harder, when to lean on the additives, and the pairings that keep the hole running.
How do you mix your gel — by the bag, or by the feel?

The gel does the work. The additives do the tuning.
HDD Gel handles the basics. Wall, suspension, cooling. On clean sand or stable ground, that's most of what you need.

When the ground gets harder, the gel doesn't change. The program around it does.

On loose, leaky ground, pair with Filter Low to seal the wall. On long bores with heavy rods, add Torque Down so the string doesn't bind. On reactive clay, Clay Control stops the swell.

Same base. Different tune for the ground.

If you're not sure what the hole needs, ring the team. We'll dial in the program before you mix the tank.
What's the trickiest ground you've drilled this year?
